title: Dance Activity: Yoga for Dancers
description: Open to all students. Provides physically skilled instruction and knowledge of yoga.

title: Dance Influencers
description: Basic characteristics and functions of dance on social media (TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube)–entertainment, entrepreneurship, self-expression, wellness, community building–by examining global dance influencers in hip hop, fitness, cheerleading, jazz, K-pop, drag, vogue, competition, ballet, Latin, Bollywood, and more.

title: First Year Seminar
description: Introduction to concepts, theories, and best current practices of dance as a contemporary art form.

title: Dancemaking Praxis I
description: Practice of compositional, generative, and performance aspects of dancemaking from classical to contemporary perspectives. Ecosystem of encouragement, learning, and support through shared processes of making dances.

title: Performance in Capstone
description: Performers in aesthetic, logistical, procedural, and theoretical considerations. Students admitted through audition will perform in capstone projects.

title: Contact Improvisation I
description: Somatic perspectives on gravity, momentum, weight sharing, and other laws of physics. Duet improvisational skills to include partnering that requires immediacy, responsiveness, and trust.

title: Introduction to Dance
description: Foundations of dance in Western civilization. Dance as art, therapy, fitness, ritual, and social discourse. Analysis of dance in film, video, and live performance with an appreciation for artistic intent, technique, and style.

title: Somatic Movement Practices I
description: Body-mind practices focused on first-person experience of movement. Awareness of sensations and perceptions are cultivated through the practice of somatic systems to include Bartenieff Fundamentals, Body-Mind Centering, and the Feldenkrais Method.

title: Performance Forum
description: Dance master classes, workshops, as related to dance performance, style, and repertoire.

title: Ballet I
description: Ballet skills for dance majors and minors emphasizing placement, coordination, ballet terminology, and technical principles.

title: Dance Technique(s) Praxis I
description: Praxis of classical, contemporary, cultural, and popular dance forms.

title: Dancemaking II
description: Continued practice of compositional, generative, and performance aspects of dancemaking from classical to contemporary perspectives. Ecosystem of encouragement, learning, and support through shared processes of making dances.

title: Dancemaking Lab I
description: Focuses on development of content, choreography and performance techniques. Student-led initiatives, creative arts research, technical production elements and dance as a way to express, envision, and enact connection, imagination and social change.

title: Dance, Popular Culture, and Identity
description: Sociocultural, political, and aesthetical functions of dance in popular culture, from Hollywood movies to Broadway musicals, television shows, YouTube, and global social media.

title: Embodied Anatomy
description: Experiential and empirical overview of human anatomy and kinesiology. Movement and awareness practices from contemplative and somatic methodologies facilitating subjective, first-person study. Objective analyses include images, models, and physical demonstrations of basic biomechanics.

title: Body Modalities
description: Alternative movement theory systems including an introduction to body modalities of yoga, Pilates, ideokinesis, Alexander and Feldenkrais techniques, Laban movement analysis and authentic movement.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Advanced Yoga for Dancer
description: Anatomical awareness, breathing and meditation techniques, and use of imagery to integrate functional and creative potential.

title: Dancemaking Praxis III
description: Traditional and contemporary methods, practices, and principles of choreography and improvisational dancemaking. Practices and orchestrations of all aspects of composition and dance performance.

title: Dancemaking Lab II
description: Focuses on development of content, choreography and performance techniques. Student-led initiatives, creative arts research, technical production elements and dance as a way to express, envision, and enact connection, imagination and social change.

title: Contact Improvisation II
description: Continuing somatic approaches to gravity, momentum, weight sharing, and other laws of physics. Further development to duet improvisational skills to include partnering that requires immediacy, responsiveness, and trust.

title: University Dance Company: Major Performance
description: Practical experience in University Dance Company including concert performances of dance repertory, production of choreographic works, presentation of master classes and workshops, and participation in major production. Students must enroll in a minimum of two semesters.

title: Video Dance Production
description: Technical applications as applied to dance and dance production. Continuation of

title: Dance History: contemporary Global Contexts
description: History of dance from early twentieth century to present in a global context. Political, economic, and cultural forces that have shaped the development of contemporary dance as an art form.

title: Dance in World Cultures
description: Dance in selected cultures; geographic, historical, social, and aesthetic factors which have shaped development and function.

title: K-pop Dance
description: An evolution of K-pop dance from the 1980s’ broadcasting backup dancers to the 2020s’ dance influencers and global dance fandom for community building, self-expression, entrepreneurship, fitness, entertainment, and youth activism on social media.

title: Dance Pedagogy
description: Teaching theory and practice as applied to dance for K-12 and adult populations.

title: Dance Practicum I
description: An introduction to the dance teaching profession. Practical field study that integrates technical and conceptual content knowledge
notes: Limit of eight units of DANCE 386A, DANCE 386B, DANCE 486A, DANCE 486B applicable to all Dance degrees.

title: Dance Practicum II
description: Building on the practical application skills and theories studied in DANCE 386A, through field observations and practice. Supervised field study integrates professional studies of technical and conceptual knowledge
notes: Limit of eight units of DANCE 386A, DANCE 386B, DANCE 486A, DANCE 486B applicable to all Dance degrees.

title: Somatic Movement Practices II
description: Continuing body-mind practices focused on first-person experience of movement. Increasing awareness of sensations and perceptions cultivated through additional practices of somatic systems to include Bartenieff Fundamentals, Body-Mind Centering, and Feldenkrais Method.

title: Dance Internship
description: Supervised practical experience in dance studio management and instruction.

title: Performance Forum
description: Dance master classes, workshops, as related to dance performance, style, repertoire.

title: Ballet II
description: Ballet skills for dance majors emphasizing turns, jumps, batterie, extended sequences, and movement quality.

title: Dance Technique(s) Praxis II
description: Advanced praxis of classical, contemporary, cultural, and popular dance forms.

title: Applied Dance Techniques II
description: Application of classical, contemporary, cultural, and popular advanced dance forms.

title: Senior Capstone
description: Fulfills the Capstone Requirements for B.F.A. candidates in the Dance major. Areas may emphasize either aspects of performance/choreography, pedagogical research and practice or dance research.

title: Digital Media Dance Production
description: Lighting, set, multi-media, and design for dance. Study of concert multi-media and production for dance.

title: Performance Writing
description: Examination of contemporary dance through the related perspectives of criticism and aesthetics. This writing-intensive course enhances critical thinking and analytical skills, and develops a vocabulary with which to examine, address, and articulate a fundamentally non-verbal art form.
notes: Not open to students with credit in DANCE 481. Satisfies the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR) for students who get a minimum grade of C or Cr. Upper-division courses should only be taken by students who have completed 60 semester units or more. In exceptional cases, a student who has completed fewer than 60 units may enroll in upper division courses.

title: Dance Practicum III
description: Builds on the practical application skills and theories studied in DANCE 386B field observation and field practice. Supervised field study integrates professional studies of technical and conceptual knowledge
notes: Limit of eight units of DANCE 386A, DANCE 386B, DANCE 486A, DANCE 486B applicable to all Dance degrees.

title: Dance Practicum IV
description: Final Practicum that focuses on student concerns as they begin realistic Early Field Experience in public schools. Emphasis on refining skills, professional ethics, and synthesizing dance knowledge with pedagogical knowledge to prepare for DANCE 453 capstone project.
notes: Final course in a series of practicum courses that fulfills the required 30 and 45 hours (depending on program) of paid or volunteer fieldwork in a California public school. Limit of eight units of DANCE 386A, DANCE 386B, DANCE 486A, DANCE 486B applicable to all Dance degrees.
